title: Tracking follow-up of incidental imaging findings: a narrative review of approaches, failure points and the patients who are missed
abstract: Background: follow-up imaging recommended for incidental findings is often not done. Aim: to describe approaches used to track these recommendations, the completion they report, where the loop breaks and which patients are missed. Methods: narrative review of reports from 2010 to 2026 in English and French, organised by failure point, with completion figures reported with their definitions and not pooled. Results and conclusions will be written after the review.
introduction: Incidental findings are common, and follow-up recommendations often go unacted. Departments can choose report codes, tracking lists, navigators, clinician alerts or letters to patients, but these have been studied in different settings with different definitions of completion.
methods: Three bibliographic databases and grey literature searched, with citation follow-up. Two radiologists screen and extract approach, setting, finding types, completion definition, failure points, resources and results for patients without a primary care clinician, emergency-only patients and patients who need an interpreter. Figures are checked against their sources; unverified leads are excluded.
results: No review data have been extracted yet. The report will present the flow of reports, a table of approaches with completion and definitions, the failure points each approach addresses, resources, and results for the groups most often missed.
discussion: The discussion will compare approaches by the links of the loop they repair, weigh the quality and comparability of the evidence, and state what it means for the department's choice.
limitations: Narrative synthesis; English and French reports only; mostly single-centre before-after evidence; completion defined differently across reports.
conclusion: To be written after the review; it will not rank approaches by a pooled figure and will cite no unverified benchmark.
reportingChecklist: SANRA items as a quality checklist for narrative reviews
summary: Narrative review draft with results left empty until extraction is complete.
